answer: A sybil-resistant agent economy can require every identity to plant a cedar-like stake: a time-locked bond that only matures after the agent completes a verifiable voyage of distinct, useful tasks across independent verifiers. Like a cedar growing slow roots in an ocean of cheap identities, the bond makes each new face expensive in time and locked capital, while duplicate behaviour across identities triggers slashing of all linked bonds, so one operator farming many faces pays many times over.
